# Background

A gene with zero observed COSMIC missense mutations at a given codon could
reflect either genuine absence of somatic selection there, or simply poor
sequencing coverage of that region across the studies contributing to
COSMIC. COSMIC aggregates variant calls from thousands of independent
historical studies with no unified capture design, so no direct per-position
coverage denominator for COSMIC itself exists, and none is likely to become
available.

gnomAD provides a large, independently sequenced cohort (v4.1: 730,947 exomes)
assembled from many different sequencing platforms, projects, and capture
kits. A gene with a genuine sequencing-coverage problem (for example, a
repetitive or GC-rich region that many capture kits struggle with) would be
expected to show reduced coverage in gnomAD as well, since gnomAD's cohort
draws on a similarly heterogeneous mix of underlying studies. Uniformly good
gnomAD coverage across a gene is therefore evidence against a systematic,
capture-driven coverage problem at that locus, and by extension makes it less
likely that COSMIC's ascertainment of the same coding sequence is
compromised for the same reason. This does not measure COSMIC's own coverage
directly, and cannot rule out COSMIC-specific gaps unrelated to general
capture difficulty, but it is a useful proxy for genes that are inherently
hard to sequence.

This check restricts to the coding sequence of each gene's MANE Select
transcript, queried directly from the gnomAD API (v4.1 exome coverage;
`gnomad_r4`, which shares its coverage data with v4.1), rather than
downloading gnomAD's full genome-wide coverage summary (many gigabytes,
almost entirely outside the ~145 genes of interest).

```{r setup, message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
library(tidyverse)
library(httr)
library(jsonlite)
theme_set(theme_bw(12))
knitr::opts_chunk$set(warning = FALSE, message = FALSE, cache = TRUE, autodep = TRUE)

DATA_DIR  <- "../../../Data"
ST2_FILE  <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "Tables/Supplementary_Table2.csv")
OUT_TABLE <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "ML_model_input/gnomad_coverage_check_informative_genes.csv")
OUT_FIG   <- file.path(DATA_DIR, "Figures/Final/Supplement/Gnomad_coverage_check.png")

GNOMAD_API <- "https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org/api"
```

# 1. Gene set

The 145 genes for which somatic data are informative (per-gene benchmarking,
count-weighted ClinVar pathogenic variants, AUC lower 95% CI > 0.6 for at
least one somatic feature -- COSMIC, sperm NanoSeq, or buccal NanoSeq
missense codon count; Results, "Somatic data predicts germline pathogenicity
in DD genes"), reproduced directly from Supplementary Table 2.

```{r genes}
st2 <- read_csv(ST2_FILE, show_col_types = FALSE) %>% filter(dataset == "clinvar_count_weighted")
qualifying_genes <- function(predictor) {
  st2 %>% filter(Predictor == predictor, !is.na(AUC_full_lower), AUC_full_lower > 0.6) %>% pull(gene)
}
genes_cosmic <- qualifying_genes("n_COSMIC_codon_count")
genes_sperm  <- qualifying_genes("n_sperm_codon_count")
genes_buccal <- qualifying_genes("n_buccal_codon_count")
genes_positive <- union(union(genes_cosmic, genes_sperm), genes_buccal)

cat("COSMIC missense codon count (AUC lower CI > 0.6):", length(genes_cosmic), "\n")
cat("Sperm NanoSeq missense codon count:", length(genes_sperm), "\n")
cat("Buccal NanoSeq missense codon count:", length(genes_buccal), "\n")
cat("Union (informative genes):", length(genes_positive), "\n")
```

# 2. gnomAD coverage query

For each gene, two GraphQL queries against the gnomAD API retrieve: (i) the
Ensembl ID of the gene's MANE Select transcript; (ii) that transcript's
coding-sequence (CDS) exon boundaries and its exome coverage profile
(binned by position, each bin giving the mean depth and the fraction of the
730,947-exome cohort with at least 1x/10x/20x coverage at that position).
Coverage bins are restricted to positions falling within a CDS exon, so that
non-coding (intronic) positions -- which are not targeted by exome capture
and are not relevant to missense-variant detection -- do not contribute to
the summary.

Over a run of ~150 genes (~300 requests), the API occasionally returns a
transient non-JSON error page instead of a normal response; a retry with
backoff resolves this in practice, so the query helper below retries up to
4 times before giving up on a gene.

```{r query-helper}
gnomad_query <- function(query, max_attempts = 4) {
  for (attempt in seq_len(max_attempts)) {
    resp <- POST(GNOMAD_API, body = list(query = query), encode = "json",
                 add_headers("Content-Type" = "application/json"))
    txt <- content(resp, as = "text", encoding = "UTF-8")
    parsed <- tryCatch(fromJSON(txt, simplifyVector = FALSE), error = function(e) NULL)
    if (!is.null(parsed)) return(parsed)
    Sys.sleep(2 * attempt)
  }
  list(errors = list(list(message = "request failed after retries")))
}

get_mane_transcript <- function(gene_symbol) {
  q <- sprintf('{ gene(gene_symbol: "%s", reference_genome: GRCh38) { mane_select_transcript { ensembl_id } } }', gene_symbol)
  d <- gnomad_query(q)
  if (!is.null(d$errors) || is.null(d$data$gene)) return(NA_character_)
  mst <- d$data$gene$mane_select_transcript
  if (is.null(mst)) NA_character_ else mst$ensembl_id
}

get_transcript_cds_coverage <- function(transcript_id) {
  q <- sprintf('{ transcript(transcript_id: "%s", reference_genome: GRCh38) {
      exons { start stop feature_type }
      coverage(dataset: gnomad_r4) { exome { pos mean over_1 over_10 over_20 } }
    } }', transcript_id)
  d <- gnomad_query(q)
  if (!is.null(d$errors) || is.null(d$data$transcript)) return(NULL)
  t <- d$data$transcript
  exons <- map_dfr(t$exons, ~ tibble(start = .x$start, stop = .x$stop, feature_type = .x$feature_type))
  cds <- exons %>% filter(feature_type == "CDS")
  cov <- map_dfr(t$coverage$exome, ~ tibble(pos = .x$pos, mean = .x$mean, over_1 = .x$over_1,
                                             over_10 = .x$over_10, over_20 = .x$over_20))
  list(cds = cds, cov = cov)
}

in_any_cds <- function(pos, cds) {
  any(pos >= cds$start & pos <= cds$stop)
}
```

```{r run-query}
coverage_summary <- map_dfr(genes_positive, function(gene) {
  tx <- get_mane_transcript(gene)
  if (is.na(tx)) return(tibble(gene = gene, transcript = NA_character_, status = "no_mane_transcript"))

  res <- get_transcript_cds_coverage(tx)
  if (is.null(res) || nrow(res$cov) == 0) return(tibble(gene = gene, transcript = tx, status = "no_coverage_data"))

  cds_bins <- res$cov %>% filter(map_lgl(pos, in_any_cds, cds = res$cds))
  if (nrow(cds_bins) == 0) return(tibble(gene = gene, transcript = tx, status = "no_cds_bins_matched"))

  cds_bins %>% summarise(
    gene = gene, transcript = tx, status = "ok",
    n_cds_bins = n(),
    mean_depth = mean(mean),
    min_bin_mean_depth = min(mean),
    pct_bins_depth_lt10 = 100 * mean(mean < 10),
    pct_bins_depth_lt20 = 100 * mean(mean < 20),
    mean_frac_over_10 = mean(over_10),
    mean_frac_over_20 = mean(over_20),
    min_frac_over_20 = min(over_20)
  )
})

cat("Genes queried:", nrow(coverage_summary), "\n")
cat("Status breakdown:\n")
print(count(coverage_summary, status))
write_csv(coverage_summary, OUT_TABLE)
```

# 3. Results

```{r table}
coverage_summary %>%
  filter(status == "ok") %>%
  arrange(mean_frac_over_20) %>%
  mutate(across(where(is.numeric), ~ round(.x, 2))) %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "gnomAD v4.1 exome coverage (CDS-restricted, MANE Select transcript) for the 145 somatic-informative genes, ordered by mean fraction of the cohort with >=20x coverage")
```

```{r figure, fig.width=8, fig.height=26}
plot_dat <- coverage_summary %>% filter(status == "ok") %>%
  mutate(gene = fct_reorder(gene, mean_frac_over_20))

fig <- ggplot(plot_dat, aes(x = mean_frac_over_20, y = gene)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 0, xend = mean_frac_over_20, y = gene, yend = gene), colour = "grey70") +
  geom_point(aes(colour = mean_depth), size = 2.5) +
  scale_colour_viridis_c(name = "Mean depth (x)") +
  scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0, 1), labels = scales::percent) +
  labs(title = "gnomAD exome coverage of the coding sequence, per gene",
       subtitle = "Mean fraction of 730,947 gnomAD v4.1 exomes with >=20x coverage, averaged across CDS positions",
       x = "Mean fraction of cohort with ≥20x coverage", y = NULL) +
  theme(axis.text.y = element_text(size = 8))
ggsave(OUT_FIG, fig, width = 8, height = 26, dpi = 300)
fig
```

# Interpretation

```{r interp-numbers}
ok <- coverage_summary %>% filter(status == "ok")
failed <- coverage_summary %>% filter(status != "ok")
outliers <- ok %>% filter(mean_frac_over_20 < 0.8) %>% arrange(mean_frac_over_20)
```

`r nrow(ok)` of `r nrow(coverage_summary)` genes queried returned usable
coverage data (`r paste(failed$gene, collapse=", ")` returned no coverage
data from the API -- `r failed$gene[1]` sits in a pseudoautosomal region,
which gnomAD's coverage endpoint does not resolve cleanly). The large
majority show good, consistent coverage: median mean depth across the
cohort is `r round(median(ok$mean_depth), 1)`x, and `r sum(ok$mean_frac_over_20 >= 0.8)`
of `r nrow(ok)` genes have a mean fraction of the cohort with at least 20x
coverage of 0.8 or higher across their coding sequence, with occasional
individual low-depth bins (most prominently in `r ok$gene[which.min(ok$min_bin_mean_depth)]`)
consistent with normal exon-boundary effects rather than a gene-wide deficit.

This is not universally true, however: `r nrow(outliers)` gene(s) fall
below that 0.8 threshold, most strikingly **`r outliers$gene[1]`**
(mean depth `r round(outliers$mean_depth[1], 1)`x; only
`r round(100 * outliers$mean_frac_over_20[1], 1)`% of the cohort reaches
20x coverage across its coding sequence) -- a pattern consistent with a
genuine, gene-wide capture difficulty rather than isolated exon-boundary
noise, and worth flagging explicitly given that `r outliers$gene[1]`
qualifies as somatic-informative via COSMIC missense codon count itself,
with an AUC lower confidence interval close to the 0.6 threshold. This
result should be read gene-by-gene (Supplementary Table 11) rather than
summarised as a single reassuring or concerning statement across all 145
genes: most genes show no indication of a coverage-driven artefact, but
this check is precisely useful because it identifies the specific
exceptions where that possibility cannot be excluded, rather than
asserting it is universally absent. This remains a proxy check throughout
and does not measure COSMIC's own coverage directly, nor rule out
COSMIC-specific ascertainment gaps unrelated to general capture
difficulty.
